arxiv-1710-00159.title: Search for low mass vector resonances decaying into quark-antiquark pairs in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-1710-00159.description: Abstract A search for narrow vector resonances decaying into quark-antiquark pairs is presented. The analysis is based on data collected in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV with the CMS detector at the LHC, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 35.9 \fbinv .

arxiv-2307-04929.title: Dual CFT on Nariai limit for Kerr-Sen-dS black holes
arxiv-2307-04929.creator: Muhammad Fitrah Alfian Rangga Sakti, Piyabut Burikham
arxiv-2307-04929.description: Abstract In this work, we study the Kerr-Sen-de Sitter black hole (BH) in the Nariai limit where the event and cosmological horizon coincide. We show that the near-horizon Kerr-Sen-de Sitter black hole in Nariai limit is a fiber over AdS 2 with an appropriate coordinate transformation, instead of fiber over dS 2 .

arxiv-2311-16909.title: Multinomial belief networks for healthcare data
arxiv-2311-16909.creator: H. C. Donker, D. Neijzen, J. de Jong, G. A. Lunter
arxiv-2311-16909.description: Abstract Healthcare data from patient or population cohorts are often characterized by sparsity, high missingness and relatively small sample sizes. In addition, being able to quantify uncertainty is often important in a medical context. To address these analytical requirements we propose a deep generative Bayesian model for multinomial count data.

arxiv-2509-07894.title: HiPhO: How Far Are (M)LLMs from Humans in the Latest High School Physics Olympiad Benchmark?
arxiv-2509-07894.creator: Fangchen Yu, Haiyuan Wan, Qianjia Cheng, Yuchen Zhang, Jiacheng Chen, Fujun Han, Yulun Wu, Junchi Yao, Ruilizhen Hu, Ning Ding, Yu Cheng, Tao Chen, Lei Bai, Dongzhan Zhou, Yun Luo, Ganqu Cui, Peng Ye
arxiv-2509-07894.description: Abstract Recently, the physical capabilities of (M)LLMs have garnered increasing attention. However, existing benchmarks for physics suffer from two major gaps: they neither provide systematic and up-to-date coverage of real-world physics competitions such as physics Olympiads, nor enable direct performance comparison with humans.

pmc-11621729.title: Screen time among preschoolers: exploring individual, familial, and environmental factors
pmc-11621729.creator: Sangha Lee, Donghee Kim, Yunmi Shin
pmc-11621729.description: Screen-based activity refers to the use of screened devices, which are changing from stationary devices such as televisions and desktop computers to newer portable devices such as smartphones and electronic tablets. The exposure of younger children to all types of screened devices has increased.

pmc-11681590.title: Determinants of Leptomeningeal Collateral Status in Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis of Observational Studies
pmc-11681590.creator: Kunyi Li, Hua Jiang, Jianping Yu, Yong Liu, Lili Zhang, Bi Ma, Shu Zhu, Yinkuang Qi, Shuang Li, Yan Huang, Yuhan Yang, Xun Xia, Lan Wen
pmc-11681590.description: BackgroundLeptomeningeal collateral status is a major determinant of outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke; however, the factors that determine collateral status are not well understood. We conducted a comprehensive systematic review and meta‐analysis to identify determinants associated with collateral status in patients with anterior circulation infarction.

pmc-12620776.title: Effects of bottle gourd moxibustion combined with umbilical therapy for cancer-related incomplete bowel obstruction on inflammatory cytokine levels
pmc-12620776.creator: Jing-Wen Wu, Li-Ping Li, Yin-Song Chen
pmc-12620776.description: BACKGROUNDCancer-induced incomplete bowel obstruction presents numerous clinical challenges, notably pain management and inflammation control. Conventional therapies provide limited relief, prompting investigation into complementary approaches. This study compares the efficacy of bottle gourd moxibustion combined with umbilical therapy (BGM-UT) plus standard palliative care vs standard Western palliative care alone in symptom alleviation and inflammation reduction.

pmc-13106813.title: Mechanistic basis for improved activity of Engineered AsCas12a
pmc-13106813.creator: Linnea Jansson-Fritzberg, Bryant Chica, Chrysa Latrick, Andrea Olland, Alexey Dementiev, Andre White, Steffen Kutter, Jean-Noel Lemercier, Steven Wolk
pmc-13106813.description: CRISPR-associated proteins (Cas) are central to gene editing, forming nuclease complexes with guide RNA to enable precise genome modification. Among numerous Cas variants, Cas9 and Cas12a are the most extensively studied. While much is known about the genomic substrates for these enzymes, less is known about the determinants of the DNA cleavage activity.

pmc-13170290.title: Precision Fc remodeling via glycosylation-competent CHO display enables ultra-selective FcγRIIIa targeting and enhanced antitumor activity
pmc-13170290.creator: Migyeong Jo, Suyeon Kim, Sanghwan Ko, Munsu Kyung, Seunghyeon Lee, Woo Hyung Ko, Wonju Lee, Sang Taek Jung
pmc-13170290.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundImproving tumor cell clearance by therapeutic antibodies remains a translational bottleneck because wild-type IgG1 Fc typically elicits suboptimal NK cell–mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC), necessitating Fc engineering to enhance activating FcγR engagement while preserving antigen specificity and manufacturability. FcγRIIIa (CD16A) is the principal activating receptor on NK cells, and its clinical relevance is underscored by the FCGR3A-158V/F polymorphism, which modulates IgG1 Fc affinity and therapeutic response.

pmc-13448485.title: Glutamate- and GABA-targeted drugs for Co-occurring bipolar and alcohol use disorders: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study of N-acetylcysteine, gabapentin, and placebo
pmc-13448485.creator: James J Prisciandaro, William H Mellick, Sara Hix, Kaiya Brand, Bryan K Tolliver, Raymond F Anton
pmc-13448485.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Forty percent of people with bipolar disorder (BD) develop alcohol use disorder (AUD), with co-occurring AUD substantially worsening the course of BD. Though efficacious treatments remain elusive, frontal glutamate and GABA dysregulation represent promising targets for intervention. This study evaluated the ability of two adjunctive medications, N-acetylcysteine (NAC) and gabapentin, to modulate glutamate and GABA (primary) and to reduce heavy drinking and depressive symptoms (exploratory) in people with BD + AUD.

pmc-13612952.title: Pathological features of fibrous proliferative lesions of the vagina in dogs
pmc-13612952.creator: Chiaki KITA, Yumi MIYAI, James K CHAMBERS, Kazuyuki UCHIDA
pmc-13612952.description: The clinical, histological, and immunohistochemical features of 26 fibrous proliferative lesions in the vagina of 14 female dogs (13 intact and 2 neutered) were examined. These lesions presented as nodular or pedunculated masses. Histopathological examination revealed that all lesions consisted of spindle- and stellate-shaped cells with mild atypia, collagenous stroma, and blood vessels. Mitotic figures were rare.

pmc-13658886.title: Comments on: Flow Cytometric Profiling Reveals Platelet Dysfunction and Impaired Immune Communication in Acute and Chronic Cerebrovascular Disease
pmc-13658886.creator: Rajesh Prasad Jayaswal, Azeem Rizvi, Javed Siddiqui, Maajid Mohi Ud Din Malik
pmc-13658886.description: ctions across acute and chronic cerebrovascular disease moves the discussion beyond platelet count and routine coagulation assays toward functional thromboimmune phenotyping. The strength of the article lies in its laboratory‐to‐clinic orientation: It invites clinical laboratories to consider whether platelet activation and platelet‐immune communication can become measurable, reproducible, and interpretable signals of neurovascular injury.
